### The positive control, layer by layer

<p align="center"><img src="{{fig:circle_depth_qwen3.5-2b.gif}}" alt="Days and months through every layer of Qwen3.5-2B (top) and its random-init twin (bottom)" width="640"></p>

- **What you see:** days and months in the top-2 principal-component plane of Qwen3.5-2B (top row) and of its random-init twin (bottom row), one frame per layer. Each frame is rotated onto the preregistered layer's plane, so the picture does not flip between frames.
- **What to notice:** in the trained model both families keep their cyclic order at almost every depth (days: cycle score {{num:mvp.posthoc.qwen3.5-2b.pc_plane_cycle.days.11.score:.2f}} at the preregistered layer) and break mainly at the final layer (days {{num:mvp.posthoc.qwen3.5-2b.pc_plane_cycle.days.23.score:.2f}}, months {{num:mvp.posthoc.qwen3.5-2b.pc_plane_cycle.months.23.score:.2f}}). The twin's points stay tangled at every layer (days {{num:mvp.posthoc.qwen3.5-2b__random.pc_plane_cycle.days.11.score:.2f}} at the preregistered layer).
- **Caveat:** the PC-plane cycle score is post-hoc and unadjusted per layer, and it also rewards an open arc (see the closed-cycle test in the results). Days and months are the positive control, not a finding about mathematics. Static version at fixed depths: [`circle_depth_qwen3.5-2b.png`](reports/figures/circle_depth_qwen3.5-2b.png).
